=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1094-1096 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The exhausted-alert check matches the marker’s blocker ID to the latest blocker comment ID, so a later blocker comment can trigger another exhausted marker and Telegram ERROR after the retry cap.
  WHY: Re-queue markers are counted across blockers, but the exhausted marker is matched only to the current blocker; reviewers consistently rated this MAJOR.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1208-1215 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The 10-page comment limit can omit a relevant blocker marker when an issue has more than 1000 comments.
  WHY: The decision logic may then miss the latest blocker; severity disagreement: Google rated this MAJOR and Grok rated it NIT, so the highest severity is used.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1116-1136 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Search results can be silently truncated at 1000 items without the watchdog detecting or reporting the truncation.
  WHY: Blocked issues may be omitted when the queried repositories have more than 1000 matching open issues; reviewer rated this MAJOR.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1196-1205 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4]
  PROBLEM: `_read_issue_comments` does not explicitly set the comment sort direction when fetching its capped pages.
  WHY: The reviewer says the current GitHub API default keeps the cap safe for finding the latest blocker, but a changed API default or different GitHub instance could alter ordering.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1741 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4]
  PROBLEM: `_cmd_queue_closed_targets` returns exit code 3 for a `RuntimeError`, unlike the other CLI subcommands’ success or input-error codes.
  WHY: Current callers treat every non-zero code as failure, but a future caller branching on exit codes could misclassify this undocumented and untested code.
- scripts/claude_issue_queue_watchdog.sh:144-145 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The validation does not check that `retry` and `retries` are integers before interpolating them into comments and Telegram messages.
  WHY: Unexpected non-numeric values from the JSON extraction could produce garbled user-visible messages; the reviewers rated this NIT.
- scripts/claude_issue_queue_watchdog.sh:182 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The Telegram alert appends `Run: ${RUN_URL}` even when `RUN_URL` is empty, leaving a dangling `Run:` line.
  WHY: The reviewers describe this as a confusing cosmetic defect; z-ai_glm-5_2 disputes the finding, stating that `RUN_URL` is set at the job level and inherited by the step.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "A re-queued issue whose label is still there after `CLAUDE_ISSUE_QUEUE_STALE_HOURS` counts as another failed retry." (README.md lines ~1346-1347)
  expected_change_site: scripts/claude_issue_route.py env_requeue_decision
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4]
  EVIDENCE: The stale-requeue path at lines 1098-1102 correctly detects a stale re-queue and returns `action="requeue"` with `reason="stale_requeue"`. The test `test_env_decision_requeues_again_when_the_fresh_session_died_silently` covers this path. However, the retry counter in this path increments `recent + 1` where `recent` counts ALL requeue markers in the window, not only those for the current blocker. If a previous stale retry's re-queue marker was for a different blocker_id, that marker still contributes to `recent`. This means a single stale retry (which legitimately doesn't consume the `max_retries` budget for the current blocker) would incorrectly push `retries_in_window` up by counting an unrelated earlier re-queue. The watchdog log would show `retry=2` when it should show `retry=1` for the current blocker chain.
- requirement: "After `CLAUDE_ISSUE_ENV_REQUEUE_MAX` (default 2) re-queues in `CLAUDE_ISSUE_ENV_REQUEUE_WINDOW_HOURS` (default 24), it posts `<!-- ai:claude-env-requeue-exhausted:v1 … -->`, sends one Telegram ERROR, and leaves the label in place."
  expected_change_site: scripts/claude_issue_route.py env_requeue_decision
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: The matcher keys on `int(exhausted.group(1)) == blocker_id`. Since a brand-new blocker comment will have a different ID than any previous exhausted marker, `alerted` will never be set to `True` based on past markers, and the retry cap will be bypassed on every cycle after the first exhaustion. Grok also notes that tests cover only same-ID replay.
- requirement: "a safe `set -euo pipefail` script that re-queues via the `claude-issue` dispatch" (implied by the watchdog's `continue-on-error: true` step and the docstring contract at scripts/claude_issue_queue_watchdog.sh:65-87)
  expected_change_site: .github/workflows/claude-issue-queue-watchdog.yml `Re-queue Claude issues blocked by an environment failure` step
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: The step sets `GH_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_ISSUE_QUEUE_TOKEN`, and `CLAUDE_ISSUE_WATCHDOG_MODE`. It fails to set `CLAUDE_ISSUE_DISPATCHER` or `CLAUDE_ISSUE_TRIGGERING_ACTOR`, causing the intake to resolve the dispatcher as `github-actions[bot]` (with an empty triggering actor), which lacks admin/write permissions on most consumer repositories, causing `authorize_target` to reject the dispatch. deepseek_deepseek-v4 calls this pass-1 task gap a false positive: the dispatch goes through `claude-issue-intake.yml`, which sets `CLAUDE_ISSUE_DISPATCHER: ${{ github.actor }}` and resolves the dispatcher as the PAT account.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4 ===
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1094-1096 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The `alerted` flag matches the exhausted marker's `blocker` field against `blocker_id`, which is the latest blocker comment's GitHub comment ID. A new environment blocker posted by a later session with a different comment ID after the exhausted marker was already written does not match the existing exhausted marker, so `alerted` stays `False` and the function returns `action="alert"` again rather than `reason="exhausted_alerted"`.
  WHY: In practice this is narrow — after an alert fires, no more re-queues happen and no fresh session is started, so no new blocker comment is posted by automation. The only trigger would be a human posting a new blocker comment, which is a deliberate intervention. However, the guard against duplicate alerts is structurally per-comment-ID rather than per-issue, so it is weaker than the documented "once per issue" contract.
- scripts/claude_issue_queue_watchdog.sh:182 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The comment body correctly guards empty `RUN_URL` with `[ -z "${RUN_URL}" ] || body+=...` (lines 168, 178), but the `tg_send_msg` call on line 182 unconditionally appends `$'\n'"Run: ${RUN_URL}"` to the message string. When `RUN_URL` is empty, the Telegram message ends with a dangling `Run: ` line.
  WHY: A cosmetic defect in the operator-facing Telegram alert; the message still conveys the critical information but the dangling `Run:` line is confusing.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1196-1205 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The function reads pages 1 through 10 of issue comments with `per_page=100` and no explicit `direction` parameter. GitHub REST API for issue comments defaults to `direction=desc` (newest first), so page 1 gives the 100 newest comments. If an issue has more than 1000 comments, pages beyond page 10 (containing the oldest comments) are skipped. Since `env_requeue_decision` takes the latest blocker comment, and the newest comments are on page 1, the 10-page cap is safe for that logic. However, the function does not pass an explicit `direction=desc` parameter, so a future API default change or a different GitHub instance could silently alter the ordering and cause the latest blocker to be missed.
  WHY: In the current GitHub API default (direction=desc), the cap is harmless for finding the latest blocker. The risk is brittleness to API default changes rather than a current bug. The 10-page cap is documented as a conscious tradeoff.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1741 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The function returns exit code 3 when `fetch_open_queue` raises a `RuntimeError`. Every other CLI subcommand returns either 0 (success) or 2 (input/parse error). Code 3 is not documented or tested, and the watchdog's `env_requeue` function treats all non-zero exits as failure regardless of code.
  WHY: Current callers do not distinguish exit codes, so no runtime failure today. A future caller branching on exit codes could misclassify the error.
- requirement: "A re-queued issue whose label is still there after `CLAUDE_ISSUE_QUEUE_STALE_HOURS` counts as another failed retry." (README.md lines ~1346-1347)
  expected_change_site: scripts/claude_issue_route.py env_requeue_decision (the `stale_retry` path at lines 1098-1102)
  Evidence of absence: The stale-requeue path at lines 1098-1102 correctly detects a stale re-queue and returns `action="requeue"` with `reason="stale_requeue"`. The test `test_env_decision_requeues_again_when_the_fresh_session_died_silently` covers this path. However, the retry counter in this path increments `recent + 1` where `recent` counts ALL requeue markers in the window, not only those for the current blocker. If a previous stale retry's re-queue marker was for a different blocker_id, that marker still contributes to `recent`. This means a single stale retry (which legitimately doesn't consume the `max_retries` budget for the current blocker) would incorrectly push `retries_in_window` up by counting an unrelated earlier re-queue. The watchdog log would show `retry=2` when it should show `retry=1` for the current blocker chain.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1208-1215 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The function reads at most the first 10 pages of comments (1000 comments total). If an issue has more than 1000 comments, the newest blocker marker might be missed if it appears on page 11 or later.
  WHY: The watchdog will incorrectly return `reason=no_blocker` for long-running issues, failing to re-queue them.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1094-1096 and 1103-1108 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The exhausted alert logic checks if the ID in the exhausted marker matches the ID of the *current* blocker comment. Since a new blocker comment will have a new, unique ID, it will never match the ID stored in previous exhausted markers.
  WHY: The watchdog will repeatedly re-queue issues and trigger Telegram alerts instead of stopping after the retry cap is reached, potentially leading to alert spam and failure to stop re-queueing.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1116-1136 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: GitHub's search API silently truncates results at 1000 items. The code does not detect truncation or warn when the query returns a partial list of candidates.
  WHY: Issues that are blocked by environment failures might not be discovered by the watchdog if the total count of open issues in the queried repositories exceeds 1000.
- requirement: "After `CLAUDE_ISSUE_ENV_REQUEUE_MAX` (default 2) re-queues in `CLAUDE_ISSUE_ENV_REQUEUE_WINDOW_HOURS` (default 24), it posts `<!-- ai:claude-env-requeue-exhausted:v1 … -->`, sends on
